label: MikroTik wAP ac LTE6 kit
description: Weatherproof dual-band 802.11ac AP that is also a full RouterOS router: 2x GbE on an IPQ-4018 switch chip, an embedded LTE Cat 6 modem, 802.3af/at PoE in at 16 W max consumption.
notes: Vendor figures from the MikroTik product page specification table, read 2026-11-19: https://mikrotik.com/product/wap_ac_lte6_kit (HTTP 200, 388,174 B) and the series hardware manual https://manual.mikrotik.com/hardware/wap-ac-kit-series/ (HTTP 200). Ethernet "10/100/1000 Ethernet ports 2"; wireless 2.4 GHz max 300 Mbit/s, 5 GHz max 867 Mbit/s; "Switch chip model IPQ-4018"; embedded modem "LTE Category 6 (300Mbit/s Downlink, 50Mbit/s Uplink)". Powering: "PoE in 802.3af/at", "PoE in input Voltage 18-57 V", "Max power consumption 16 W", "Max power consumption without attachments 10 W"; the manual repeats "Ethernet port accepts 802.3af/at PoE 18-57 V DC. The power consumption under maximum load can reach 16 W." Routing: the product page states "RouterOS license 4" and "you can use the device as a wired router with LTE backup via the Micro SIM slot", and RouterOS DHCP is "both server and client parts" (https://help.mikrotik.com/docs/spaces/ROS/pages/24805500/DHCP), so dhcp-server/dhcp-client are this OS's own features and level 4 is the full WISP licence. Three defects corrected. (1) The spec declared no l2-forward, so its two GbE ports could not be bridged - the vendor prints a switch chip and a "Bridging, none (fast path)" throughput row (162.5 kpps / 1973.4 Mbps) next to the routing row. (2) The spec declared nat but not dhcp-server/dhcp-client, the only one of 306 NAT-capable MikroTik entries so configured; `ip dhcp pool lan` was refused with "% ... cannot serve DHCP", so a wAP used as the site gateway could not lease an address to anything behind it. (3) PoE-in was declared 802.3af only at 12.95 W while the vendor prints "802.3af/at" and 16 W max consumption - the declared class ceiling was below the box's own published draw, so a PoE-powered wAP was budgeted 3 W short. All three are additions, verified against siblings on the same OS (devices/mikrotik/hap-ac2.json carries l2-forward + dhcp-server + dhcp-client). wwan0 is left at 50M on purpose: Cat 6 uplink is 50 Mbit/s and the catalogue uses that LTE class figure consistently (devices/mikrotik/chateau-lte18-ax.json is 50M too), so the vendor's 300 Mbit/s downlink marketing figure does not replace it.
